note: Allow-lists for sanitized HTML stems and SVG diagrams. No author JavaScript. Apply on ingest and again before display.

html.notes: Headings start at h2 (the page already has an h1). Anchors may use https, http, #fragment, or a same-site path starting with /. No javascript: or data: links.

svg.href_rule: Fragment only, starting with #. Same as SecurityHardeningService::sanitizeSvgContent.

data_image.allowed_only_if: meta.allow_data_image is true and meta.data_image_justification is a non-empty string that explains why an https or /storage image cannot be used.

same: Allowed SVG element set is the same list (compared case-insensitively).
DOCTYPE and ENTITY declarations are rejected.
Document must be well-formed XML with an svg root.
Non-SVG namespaces are rejected or stripped.
href and xlink:href must be fragment-only (#...).
javascript:, vbscript:, expression(), @import, and style url() (except same-document #) are forbidden.
script and foreignObject are not in the allowed element list, so they are dropped.
differences: The PHP sanitizer has no explicit attribute allow-list: it keeps unknown attributes unless they are on* or have a dangerous value. v2 is stricter and only allows the attributes listed here.

The PHP sanitizer blocks every data: URI. v2 also blocks data: by default, but may allow a data:image raster only when meta.allow_data_image is true and a justification is present. Default is still deny.
The PHP method covers SVG only. v2 also defines an HTML stem allow-list (headings, lists, emphasis, tables, code). HTML is not handled by sanitizeSvgContent.
v2 forbids the style element explicitly. The PHP list already omits it, so a style element would be removed there too.
v2 validation reports a failure. The PHP method returns stripped markup or throws. Importers should still run sanitizeSvgContent on the server at ingest, even if this file already passed.
